title: Wisdom Calls Out to Everyone
overview: Wisdom, pictured as a woman, calls out in public, describes what she offers, and says she was with the LORD when he made the world.

parts.label: Wisdom calls in public (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: Wisdom stands on the heights, at crossroads and at the city gate, the busiest places, where business and court cases happened. She calls to everyone, even the naive and foolish, so no one is left out.

parts.label: Her words are straight (vv. 6-11)
parts.note: She says nothing she teaches is twisted or deceptive, and it makes sense to anyone willing to think it through. Her teaching is worth more than silver, gold or jewels.

parts.label: What wisdom brings (vv. 12-21)
parts.note: Wisdom goes with practical good sense and with respect for the LORD, which shows itself in turning away from pride, evil and lying speech. Good rulers govern by her, and those who seek her gain lasting riches and honor, which many readers take to mean good character as well as wealth.

parts.label: Wisdom before creation (vv. 22-29)
parts.note: Wisdom says the LORD brought her forth first, before seas, mountains and sky, and she was there when he set limits for the waters. Many readers take this to mean wisdom shaped how the world was made, though the Hebrew word in verse 22 can mean either "made" or "possessed," and scholars debate which.

parts.label: Delight at God's side (vv. 30-31)
parts.note: She is beside God either as a skilled builder or as a delighted child, because the Hebrew word is unclear, and she takes joy in the world and in people. Christians later read this passage in light of Jesus, seeing him as God's Word present at creation.

parts.label: Listen and live (vv. 32-36)
parts.note: Wisdom pictures the wise as people who wait at her door every day, eager to hear her. Finding her means life and the LORD's favor, while missing her harms you, and rejecting her is like choosing death.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether Wisdom here is simply a poetic picture of God's own wisdom or a deliberate early portrait of Christ.
think: When you face a hard decision, where do you actually turn for wisdom, and how do you tell whether that source deserves your trust?
